source_text:
(71) Στίχ. β΄. Καὶ τὴν προνομὴν τῶν κτηνῶν προνομεύσεις σεαυτῷ.
Ἐπειδὴ οὐκ ἔδει ὡς ἐν τῇ Ἱεριχὼ τὰ πάντα ἀνατεθῆναι.
(72) Στίχ. κς΄. Καὶ ἐξέτεινεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν γαισὸν, καὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ.
Ἔμενε γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτεταμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα· ἵνα, θεασάμενοι οἱ τῆς ἐνέδρας, προκαταλάβωνται τὴν πόλιν.
thought_title: Plunder at Ai and Joshua's outstretched spear
orientation: Origen is explaining two verses from Joshua: the command about plundering livestock at Ai, and Joshua holding out his spear and hand as a signal.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 2. And the plunder of the cattle you shall plunder for yourself. Since it was not necessary, as in Jericho, for all things to be devoted. Verse 26. And Joshua stretched out the spear, and his hand. For Joshua remained having his hand stretched out; so that, when those of the ambush saw it, they might seize the city first.

choices.english: the plunder of the cattle you shall plunder for yourself
choices.why: Keeps the cognate noun-verb construction of the Greek, preserving the emphasis on plunder as the action and object.
rejected: you shall take the cattle as plunder for yourself
you shall plunder the cattle for yourself

choices.why: Matches the glossary sense of devoting to destruction as belonging to God, and contrasts with the plunder allowed at Ai.
Uses the glossary rendering for the weapon Joshua holds out as a signal.
Renders the compound verb's force of taking the city before others, matching the purpose clause.

bible_refs.note: Καὶ τὴν προνομὴν τῶν κτηνῶν προνομεύσεις σεαυτῷ
Καὶ ἐξέτεινεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν γαισὸν, καὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ

pass_b_english: "And the plunder of the cattle you shall plunder for yourself" (Joshua 8:2). This was because it was not necessary for everything to be devoted as it had been at Jericho.
"And Joshua stretched out the spear, and his hand" (Joshua 8:26). For Joshua remained with his hand stretched out, so that when those of the ambush saw it, they might seize the city first.
